## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect remains open: `refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored digest of a tracked file that was edited by hand, which defeats the edit detection the PR body says existing fingerprints provide.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`, which update the JSON fingerprint manifest for named files. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py` to cover both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Stop refresh from overwriting digests of edited tracked files — If you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was edited by hand, it replaces the original digest with the edited file's digest, so `verify` then returns True. Line 17 assigns `entries[name]` without checking `name not in entries`, unlike `register_new_files` at line 24. The only refresh test (`tests/test_integrity.py:39`) keeps `tracked.txt` unchanged, so it cannot catch this. — A hand edit to a tracked file is silently accepted whenever that file is included in a refresh after new files are added. — Fix: Either skip names already in `entries` (as `register_new_files` does), or document that refresh accepts current contents and add an edited-file case to `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries`.
